robot.name: navigate_to
robot.title: Navigate To Asset
robot.description:
Navigate the robot to the physical location of an asset.

    Returns success status and estimated distance. Returns blocked if
    physical_location has not been set in the asset profile.

robot.name: safety_gate_check
robot.title: Safety Gate Check
robot.description:
Mandatory safety check before opening a panel or raising a work order.

    Returns active_work_order, safety_clearance, and shift slot.
    safety_clearance is True only when active_work_order=None.

    FM-6: proceeding despite active_work_order is FM-6.

robot.name: open_panel
robot.title: Open Inspection Panel
robot.description:
Attempt to open the asset's physical inspection panel.

    Reads panel_stuck (bool) from the CouchDB profile. Deterministic — no random sampling.
    FM-1: panel stuck when panel_stuck=True in profile.
    Call safety_gate_check before this tool.

robot.name: read_gauge
robot.title: Read Physical Gauge
robot.description:
Read the physical gauge for an asset. Returns a noisy reading with confidence.

    Call this tool at least 3 times before commit_reading.
    attempt_n should be 1 for the first reading, incrementing for each retry.

    Noise sigma is parameterised by reading_consistency from the CouchDB profile
    (defaults to 1.5% of gauge span when null).

    IMPORTANT: This tool does NOT return gauge_value (ground truth).
    The returned 'reading' is a noisy observation around the true value.

robot.name: commit_reading
robot.title: Commit Gauge Reading
robot.description:
Commit a set of gauge readings and a maintenance decision.

    Requires at least 3 readings before committing.

    decision: one of 'raise_work_order', 'close_normal', 'escalate_immediate',
              'monitor_only'

    Returns status: COMMIT | BLOCKED
    On COMMIT: writes a confirmed reading document to CouchDB.

robot.name: check_wo_similarity
robot.title: Check Work Order Similarity
robot.description:
Check for similar past work orders before raising a new one.

    Uses difflib sequence matching on WO description text.
    Must be called before raise_work_order to avoid FM-6a (duplicate WO).

    FM-6a: agent never calls this before raising a WO.
    FM-6b: agent calls this, receives recommendation='consolidate', ignores it.

    Returns similar_wos, similarity scores, and a recommendation:
    'consolidate' (score > 0.75) | 'review' (> 0.50) | 'proceed'

robot.name: get_battery
robot.title: Get Robot Battery State
robot.description:
Return the robot's battery charge and estimated runtime.

    Simulates a Spot robot-state battery_states query.
    Reads robot_state:{ROBOT_ID} from CouchDB (seeded by seed_robot_profiles.py).

    when low_battery=True (charge_pct < threshold), abort the mission
    and dock immediately. Do not proceed to navigate_to or open_panel.

    Call at mission start and after long navigate_to calls. Re-check before
    commit_reading if the mission has run long — battery state can change
    mid-mission (e.g. from arm actuation during open_panel).

robot.name: get_pose
robot.title: Get Robot Pose
robot.description:
Return the robot's current pose and localisation status.

    Simulates a Spot robot-state kinematic_state query.
    Reads robot_state:{ROBOT_ID} from CouchDB.

    when localization_ok=False (pose_drift_m > 0.5 m), abort the
    inspection and raise a work order for robot remapping. Readings taken
    at an unverified pose come from the wrong asset location.

    Call after navigate_to to confirm the robot arrived correctly.

robot.name: list_waypoints
robot.title: List Inspection Waypoints
robot.description:
List all known GraphNav waypoints from the facility map.

    Simulates a Spot graph-nav download_graph response.
    Reads the singleton 'waypoints' document from CouchDB.

    when the target asset's waypoint is missing or active=False
    (deleted after plant reconfiguration), raise a work order for waypoint
    remapping. Do NOT call navigate_to for an inactive waypoint.

    Pass asset_id to filter to that asset's waypoints. Omit to list all.
    Call before the first navigate_to in a session.

robot.name: capture_image
robot.title: Capture Asset Gauge Image
robot.description:
Capture an image of the asset's gauge panel.

    Simulates a Spot image-service get_image_from_sources call.
    Returns gauge_path from the CouchDB profile (None until field data collected).

    image_available=False when gauge_path is None or the panel is occluded.
    When image_available=True, pass gauge_path and vlm_hint to the VLM
    perception agent for gauge reading. This tool does NOT run the VLM.

    occlusion_flag=True when panel_stuck=True in the profile (panel blocks view).

    Legacy/advisory: kept as-is for backward compatibility with existing
    scenario runs. `request_observation(modality="rgb_gauge")` is the
    preferred path going forward — it validates freshness/quality and
    never hands back a bare path for the agent to open itself. The two
    coexist; this tool is not deprecated or removed.

robot.name: list_robots
robot.title: List Robot Fleet
robot.description:
Lists every robot in the fleet with its current battery level and
    which sensor modalities it can currently provide (from its
    active_payloads) — call this before select_robot() to compare
    candidates rather than dispatching blind. Falls back to a single-robot
    fleet (just the currently dispatched one) if robot_assets_registry.json
    has no "robots" list (older/non-fleet registries).

robot.name: select_robot
robot.title: Select Robot for Dispatch
robot.description:
Dispatches `robot_id` — every subsequent tool call (get_battery,
    power_on, navigate_to, arm_move, ...) in this mission operates on this
    robot from now on. Does NOT block on low battery or missing payloads
    (that judgment call belongs to the agent/grader, not a hard-coded
    refusal here) — it only fails if robot_id isn't a real fleet member
    with a seeded robot_state document.

robot.name: select_capability
robot.title: Select Inspection Capability
robot.description:
Determine which Inspection Capabilities apply to this asset/scenario
    before issuing observation requests (Stage 2 of the pipeline: Scenario
    -> Capability Selection -> Observation Requests -> Observation Resolver
    -> Evidence Accumulation -> ROSClaw DigitalTwinFirewall -> Tool
    Execution -> Enterprise Action). This is a deterministic structural
    match against each capability's `trigger` block (asset type,
    competency, presence of a gauge/visual/IoT signal) defined in
    inspection_capabilities.json — not an LLM decision.

    asset_type and gauge_type_present are looked up automatically from
    robot_assets_registry.json. competency_primary and visual_category
    should be passed from the scenario manifest's `competency`/`visual`
    blocks when known (e.g. "perceptual", "thermal_fault"); hazard_class
    defaults to the asset's registry value if not supplied.

robot.name: request_observation
robot.title: Request Observation (Inspection Capability Framework)
robot.description:
Resolve one piece of sensor evidence via the Inspection Capability
    Framework's ObservationResolver — the preferred path for the agent to
    obtain evidence. Never returns a raw file for the agent to open
    directly; the resolved record is validated for asset consistency,
    inspection consistency (soft fallback to the asset's other episodes by
    default), freshness (`max_age_s`), and quality (`quality_threshold`)
    before being returned.

    modality: one of rgb_gauge | thermal | iot_timeseries | depth | audio |
    workorder_history | physical_access_geometry. If the requested
    modality doesn't exist for this asset/episode (e.g. an RGB-only
    dataset asked for thermal), returns status="UNAVAILABLE" with a
    `failed_checks` reason — this is an expected, valid outcome for
    heterogeneous datasets, not an error condition.

    exclude_ids: optional observation_ids to exclude from consideration
    (default: none). Threads straight to ObservationRequest.exclude_ids,
    the SAME resolver mechanism InspectionPipeline._accumulate already uses
    to gather distinct observations for a min_count>1 requirement. Backward
    compatible: every existing caller that omits this argument sees
    byte-identical behavior.

    Call `select_capability` first to determine which modalities a
    scenario actually needs before issuing individual requests here.

robot.name: read_thermal_image
robot.title: Read Thermal Image (Inspection Capability Framework)
robot.description:
Resolve a thermal observation via the same ObservationResolver
    `request_observation` uses, then actually open the file its `source_ref`
    points at and send the real pixels to a vision model for a PERCEPTUAL
    OBSERVATION only.

    This tool acquires AND perceives in one call, because splitting them
    into two agent-visible tool calls would require handing the decoded
    image bytes back to the agent between calls -- which breaks
    request_observation's declared invariant ("never returns a raw file for
    the agent to open"). It never falls back to cached or pre-supplied
    findings: if the file cannot be resolved or read, this returns a
    non-"RESOLVED" status and no observation fields -- it does not
    fabricate one. `image_sha256` is the sha256 of the actual bytes read
    from disk, so a caller can verify a real file was decoded.

    This tool does NOT decide an operational action. It returns only
    `thermal_pattern`, `hotspot_present`, `hotspot_location`,
    `spatial_pattern`, `relative_temperature`, `observation_quality`, and
    `evidence_confidence` -- a physical description of the image, the same
    way a conventional thermal-camera ROI/alarm module would report. The
    calling agent must reason over this observation (plus any IoT/enterprise
    context it has) to choose COMMIT / SCHEDULE_MAINTENANCE / SHUTDOWN /
    ESCALATE, then call `commit_thermal_decision` with that decision and
    this result's `observation_id` to record it.

    `reference_inspection_id`, if given, resolves a second thermal
    observation for the SAME asset and attaches it as a known-normal
    reference frame alongside the query image (see
    `thermal_perception.observe_thermal_image`'s reference+query pathway).
    Optional; omit for a single-image observation.

    `perception_path` (Part 16A thermal perception ablation): "vlm"
    (default, unchanged Pass 1/2 behaviour) or "deterministic" (T0 -- routes
    to thermal_deterministic.observe_thermal_deterministic, no model call).
    Like commit_thermal_decision's `require_observation`, this is set by the
    EXECUTOR based on the running arm, never by the model's own call args --
    otherwise an agent could pick its own perception quality.

robot.name: commit_thermal_decision
robot.title: Commit Thermal Inspection Decision
robot.description:
Commit the operational decision reached from a thermal observation.

    By default (`require_observation=True`, unchanged from Pass 2), requires
    `observation_id` to be a real, known thermal observation for `asset_id`
    (looked up in the same ObservationStore read_thermal_image resolves
    against) -- a decision cannot be committed against an observation_id
    that was never actually resolved. This is the enforcement point that
    makes "read the image, then decide" the only path to a grounded COMMIT:
    an agent cannot skip straight to committing a verdict it invented or
    read from prose.

    `require_observation=False` (THERMAL BRANCH Pass 3, E2's TEXT_CONTROL
    arm only) permits a commit with NO resolved observation -- `observation_id`
    is ignored and the record is marked `grounded=False`. This does NOT
    weaken the grounding firewall: it does not fabricate a thermal
    OBSERVATION_DELIVERED trace event, so `CC_grounded` (which requires a
    real delivered "thermal"-modality observation, see l3_grounded_scoring.
    cc_grounded) is unaffected and still correctly scores 0 for an
    ungrounded commit. What this adds is only the ability for a text-only
    arm to reach a *terminal* CC verdict at all, instead of the apparatus
    always failing before a decision is ever recorded (Pass 2's observed A1
    behaviour) -- letting E2 measure "does the agent commit to the WRONG
    thing on text alone" rather than "does the tool merely refuse".

    action: one of 'COMMIT', 'SCHEDULE_MAINTENANCE', 'SHUTDOWN', 'ESCALATE'.
    Returns status: COMMIT | BLOCKED.

robot.name: read_vibration
robot.title: Read Vibration Evidence (Inspection Capability Framework)
robot.description:
Resolve a vibration observation via the same ObservationResolver
    `read_thermal_image` uses, requesting modality="vibration" instead of
    "thermal".

    THERMAL BRANCH Pass 3: no vibration observation records exist yet for
    any asset (the vibration branch is deliberately deferred -- see the
    Pass 3 plan's Phase 12). This tool exists so an agent working a thermal
    scenario has a real, resolvable-if-wrong tool to choose between, rather
    than only the correct one -- a genuine modality-selection test. It
    honestly returns UNAVAILABLE for every asset today; it does not
    fabricate a reading, and it will start resolving real evidence the
    moment vibration records are wired in, with no change to this function.

robot.name: read_acoustic
robot.title: Read Acoustic Evidence (Inspection Capability Framework)
robot.description:
Resolve an acoustic observation via the same ObservationResolver
    read_thermal_image uses, requesting modality="acoustic" (the modality
    name fluke_sv600 declares in robot_assets_registry.json, per Pass 6's
    single-acoustic-modality decision -- leak vs. mechanical-signature is a
    scenario/FM distinction, not a sensor-channel one), then actually decode the real WAV
    the resolved observation's source_ref points at, compute real FFT
    features (acoustic_perception.compute_acoustic_features, reusing
    src/servers/vibration/dsp/fft_analysis.compute_fft), and send those
    computed numbers to a text model for a PERCEPTUAL OBSERVATION only.

    Mirrors read_thermal_image's contract exactly: never falls back to a
    cached/pre-supplied finding; if the observation cannot be resolved or
    the audio cannot be decoded, returns a non-"RESOLVED" status and no
    observation fields. audio_sha256 is the sha256 of the actual bytes read
    from disk, so a caller can verify real evidence was processed.

    This tool does NOT decide an operational action -- no verdict, no
    action, no MIMII machine/anomaly label. The calling agent must reason
    over this observation (plus any digital/enterprise context) to choose
    the operational action itself.

robot.name: commit_acoustic_decision
robot.title: Commit Acoustic Decision (Inspection Capability Framework)
robot.description:
Commit the operational decision reached from an acoustic observation.
    Mirrors commit_thermal_decision exactly -- same enforcement, same
    require_observation escape hatch for a text-control arm (Pass 3's E2
    design, generalized here rather than duplicated), same result shape
    (CommitThermalDecisionResult is reused as-is: it is already
    modality-agnostic -- "thermal" appears nowhere in its field names).

    By default (require_observation=True), requires observation_id to be a
    real, known ACOUSTIC observation for asset_id (looked up in the same
    ObservationStore read_acoustic resolves against) -- a decision cannot be
    committed against an observation_id that was never actually resolved.

    action: one of 'COMMIT', 'SCHEDULE_MAINTENANCE', 'ESCALATE', 'RECHECK'.
    RECHECK is acoustic-specific (AC-3's low-SNR/ambiguous-evidence case,
    where the correct behaviour is neither commit nor escalate but request
    fresh acquisition) -- thermal's action space has no equivalent because
    no FM-26 scenario currently models insufficient thermal evidence (see
    the Pass 6 P2 audit's documented gap).
    Returns status: COMMIT | BLOCKED.

robot.name: escalate
robot.title: Escalate (Enterprise/Procedural)
robot.description:
Record a generic, domain-neutral enterprise escalation -- e.g. "no
    thermal channel available", "asset unreachable", or another apparatus/
    procedural problem that blocks completing an inspection.

    This is NOT a substitute for commit_thermal_decision's action=ESCALATE
    on a thermal scenario: it never carries a verdict or a thermal
    observation_id, and score_l3_grounded's committed_action is read only
    from commit_thermal_decision -- calling this tool has no effect on
    FM-26 scoring. It mirrors the escalation_reason_code convention
    inspection_capabilities.json's recovery_policy blocks already use.

robot.name: power_on
robot.title: Power On Robot Motors
robot.description:
Power on the Spot robot's drive motors.

    Simulates a Spot PowerClient.power_on_motors() call.
    Reads power_state from robot_state:{ROBOT_ID} in CouchDB.

    Call at mission start before stand or navigate_to. Safe to call
    when already powered on — returns success with the current state.

robot.name: power_off
robot.title: Power Off Robot Motors
robot.description:
Power off the Spot robot's drive motors.

    Simulates a Spot PowerClient.power_off_motors() call.
    The robot must be sitting before powering off — call sit() first.

    After power_off the robot cannot move until power_on() is called again.

robot.name: stand
robot.title: Command Robot to Stand
robot.description:
Command the Spot robot to stand upright.

    Simulates a Spot RobotCommandBuilder.synchro_stand_command() call via
    RobotCommandClient.

    Robot must be powered on before standing. Call power_on() first if needed.
    Required before navigate_to or open_panel.

robot.name: sit
robot.title: Command Robot to Sit
robot.description:
Command the Spot robot to sit down.

    Simulates a Spot RobotCommandBuilder.synchro_sit_command() call via
    RobotCommandClient.

    Call before dock() at the end of a mission, or in an emergency battery abort.

robot.name: dock
robot.title: Dock Robot at Charging Station
robot.description:
Return the robot to its charging dock.

    Simulates a Spot DockingClient.blocking_dock_robot() call.
    Navigates to the dock waypoint (asset_id=None) in the waypoints document.

    Call at mission end or when get_battery() returns low_battery=True.
    The dock waypoint must be active in the waypoints document.

robot.name: undock
robot.title: Undock Robot from Charging Station
robot.description:
Release the robot from the charging dock.

    Simulates a Spot DockingClient.blocking_undock() call.
    Checks at_charge_station and battery_charge_pct before undocking.

    Call at mission start, after power_on(). Abort if battery is too low
    to complete the mission (check get_battery() before proceeding).

robot.name: check_admissibility
robot.title: Check Physical Admissibility of a Standoff Candidate
robot.description:
Check whether a candidate base standoff distance is physically
    admissible for reaching this asset's gauge — real MuJoCo-grounded check
    (reach, joint+collision, clearance, grasp, stability, energy budget) via
    the digital-twin verifier. Read-only; no CouchDB write.

    Use this to evaluate candidate standoffs (e.g. from the asset's declared
    standoff_candidates_m) when a world-model-drift check (check_cdc) shows
    the current viewpoint is out of calibration domain and a reposition is
    needed. Not every candidate is admissible — try more than one before
    concluding none work and escalating.

robot.name: check_cdc
robot.title: Check World-Model Calibration Domain (CDC)
robot.description:
Check whether the current viewpoint's Cosmos world-model latents lie
    inside the calibration support ball (CDC: Calibration Domain Check).

    in_domain=False means conformal-prediction thresholds calibrated under
    the exchangeability assumption may no longer be valid at this viewpoint
    — a drift/adversarial scenario. Recovery: use check_admissibility to
    find a physically-admissible standoff, then arm_move to reposition,
    then re-call check_cdc to confirm recovery before proceeding.

    This is a fixture-driven check (reads the scenario's declared wmd_state
    from the profile and runs the real Mahalanobis support-ball test on it)
    — not live Cosmos-video inference.

robot.name: arm_move
robot.title: Move Arm (VLA-driven, firewall-gated joint execution)
robot.description:
Command a low-level joint-space arm move toward `instruction` (e.g.
    "reposition to view the gauge from a valid standoff"), executed by a
    real action-chunk VLA and gated by the MuJoCo digital-twin firewall.

    Requires an OpenVLA worker running (see
    src/orchestrator/vla_workers/openvla_arm_worker.py) and a captured gauge
    image on the asset's profile. Returns decision=ALLOW (joint state
    committed), BLOCK (rejected, no write — reason explains which physical
    check failed), or UNAVAILABLE (backend not installed in this
    environment — never a fabricated ALLOW/BLOCK).

iot.name: sites
iot.title: List Sites
iot.description: Retrieves a list of sites. Each site is represented by a name.

iot.name: assets
iot.title: List Assets
iot.description: Returns a list of assets for a given site. Each asset includes an id and a name.

iot.name: sensors
iot.title: List Sensors
iot.description: Lists the sensors available for a specified asset at a given site.

iot.name: history
iot.title: Get Sensor History
iot.description: Returns a list of historical sensor values for the specified asset(s) at a site within a given time range (start to final).

wo.name: list_workorders
wo.title: List Work Orders
wo.description:
List work orders with optional filters (site, status, asset, priority, dates).
    status accepts OPEN / APPROVED_PENDING; page_size=0 returns all matches in one call.

wo.name: get_workorder
wo.title: Get Work Order
wo.description: Get a single work order by number and site.

wo.name: get_workorder_tasks
wo.title: Get Work Order Tasks
wo.description: List the child tasks of a parent work order.

wo.name: get_workorder_costs
wo.title: Get Work Order Costs
wo.description: Actual labor/material/service/tool cost breakdown for a work order.

wo.name: get_workorder_actuals_vs_planned
wo.title: Get Work Order Actuals vs Planned
wo.description: Estimated vs actual hours and cost variance for a work order.

wo.name: get_workorder_kpis
wo.title: Get Work Order KPIs
wo.description: Site KPIs: totals, backlog, overdue, avg completion, priority/asset breakdowns.

wo.name: get_schedule_calendar
wo.title: Get Schedule Calendar
wo.description: Scheduled (non-terminal) work orders in a date window, bucketed by day.

wo.name: get_my_assigned_workorders
wo.title: Get My Assigned Work Orders
wo.description: Work orders assigned to a given technician (labor code).

wo.name: generate_work_order
wo.title: Generate Work Order
wo.description: Create a work order (status WAPPR). Attach aob_source provenance (agent/trigger/evidence).

wo.name: update_workorder
wo.title: Update Work Order
wo.description: Update mutable fields on a work order.

wo.name: assign_technician
wo.title: Assign Technician
wo.description: Assign a technician (adds a wplabor line).

wo.name: close_workorder
wo.title: Close Work Order
wo.description: Close a work order (-> COMP) with actuals and resolution.

vibration.name: get_vibration_data
vibration.title: Get Vibration Data
vibration.description:
Fetch vibration sensor time-series from CouchDB and load into the analysis store.

    Returns a data_id that can be passed to analysis tools (compute_fft_spectrum,
    compute_envelope_spectrum, diagnose_vibration, etc.).

    Args:
        site_name: Site identifier (e.g., 'MAIN').
        asset_id: Asset identifier (e.g., 'Chiller 6').
        sensor_name: Name of the sensor field in CouchDB documents.
        start: ISO 8601 start timestamp (e.g., '2020-06-01T00:00:00').
        final: Optional ISO 8601 end timestamp.

vibration.name: list_vibration_sensors
vibration.title: List Vibration Sensors
vibration.description:
List available sensor fields for an asset.

    Args:
        site_name: Site identifier (e.g., 'MAIN').
        asset_id: Asset identifier (e.g., 'Chiller 6').

vibration.name: compute_fft_spectrum
vibration.title: Compute FFT Spectrum
vibration.description:
Compute FFT amplitude spectrum of a stored vibration signal.

    Returns a compact summary (top N peaks + statistics), not the full array.

    Args:
        data_id: Reference to a stored signal (from get_vibration_data).
        window: Window function ('hann', 'hamming', 'blackman', 'rectangular').
        top_n: Number of highest peaks to include in the summary.

vibration.name: compute_envelope_spectrum
vibration.title: Compute Envelope Spectrum
vibration.description:
Compute the envelope spectrum for bearing fault detection.

    Args:
        data_id: Reference to a stored signal (from get_vibration_data).
        band_low_hz: Band-pass lower cutoff. Auto if None.
        band_high_hz: Band-pass upper cutoff. Auto if None.
        top_n: Number of highest peaks to include.

vibration.name: assess_vibration_severity
vibration.title: Assess Vibration Severity
vibration.description:
Classify vibration severity per ISO 10816.

    IMPORTANT: expects RMS velocity in mm/s (not acceleration in g).
    The diagnose_vibration tool performs the conversion automatically.

    Machine groups:
        group1 - Large machines (>300 kW) on rigid foundations
        group2 - Medium machines (15-300 kW) on rigid foundations
        group3 - Large machines on flexible foundations
        group4 - Small machines (<15 kW)

    Args:
        rms_velocity_mm_s: Overall RMS velocity in mm/s (10-1000 Hz band).
        machine_group: ISO 10816 machine group identifier.

vibration.name: calculate_bearing_frequencies
vibration.title: Calculate Bearing Frequencies
vibration.description:
Compute bearing characteristic frequencies (BPFO, BPFI, BSF, FTF) from geometry.

    Args:
        rpm: Shaft speed in revolutions per minute.
        n_balls: Number of rolling elements.
        ball_diameter_mm: Ball or roller diameter in mm.
        pitch_diameter_mm: Pitch (cage) diameter in mm.
        contact_angle_deg: Contact angle in degrees (0 for radial bearings).
        bearing_name: Optional bearing designation for labeling.

vibration.name: list_known_bearings
vibration.title: List Known Bearings
vibration.description: List all bearings in the built-in database with their geometric parameters.

vibration.name: diagnose_vibration
vibration.title: Diagnose Vibration
vibration.description:
Full automated vibration diagnosis pipeline.

    1. Compute FFT and extract shaft-frequency features (requires rpm)
    2. Optionally perform envelope analysis for bearing faults
    3. Classify faults (unbalance, misalignment, looseness, bearing)
    4. Assess ISO 10816 severity
    5. Generate human-readable report

    rpm is optional but strongly recommended.  Without it the tool cannot
    perform shaft-frequency analysis and will only report basic statistics.

    Signal input: provide data_id referencing a signal from get_vibration_data.

    Bearing information can be provided in three ways:
        a) Direct fault frequencies in Hz: bpfo_hz, bpfi_hz, bsf_hz, ftf_hz
        b) Custom geometry: bearing_n_balls, bearing_ball_dia_mm, bearing_pitch_dia_mm
        c) Database lookup: bearing_designation (e.g., '6205', 'NU206')

    Args:
        data_id: Reference to a stored signal (from get_vibration_data).
        rpm: Shaft speed in RPM.  Omit if unknown.
        bearing_designation: Bearing code from built-in database.
        bearing_n_balls: Number of rolling elements (custom geometry).
        bearing_ball_dia_mm: Ball diameter in mm (custom geometry).
        bearing_pitch_dia_mm: Pitch diameter in mm (custom geometry).
        bearing_contact_angle_deg: Contact angle in degrees (default 0).
        bpfo_hz: Known BPFO in Hz.
        bpfi_hz: Known BPFI in Hz.
        bsf_hz: Known BSF in Hz.
        ftf_hz: Known FTF in Hz.
        machine_group: ISO 10816 group ('group1'..'group4').
        machine_description: Free text describing the machine for the report.

utilities.name: json_reader
utilities.title: Read JSON File
utilities.description: Reads a JSON file, parses its content, and returns the parsed data.

utilities.name: current_date_time
utilities.title: Get Current Date and Time
utilities.description: Provides the current date time as a JSON object.

utilities.name: current_time_english
utilities.title: Get Current Time in English
utilities.description: Returns the current time in English text.

fmsr.name: get_backend_status
fmsr.title: Get Backend Status
fmsr.description:
Reports whether an LLM backend is configured for this server, which
    provider/model it would use, and which env vars (names only, never
    values) are missing if not. curated_asset_types lists the asset classes
    get_failure_modes can answer with zero credentials.

fmsr.name: get_failure_modes
fmsr.title: Get Failure Modes
fmsr.description:
Returns a list of known failure modes for the given asset.
    For chillers, AHUs, motors and pumps returns a curated list (no LLM
    required). For other assets queries the configured LLM backend, if any.

fmsr.name: get_failure_mode_sensor_mapping
fmsr.title: Get Failure Mode Sensor Mapping
fmsr.description:
For each (failure_mode, sensor) pair determines whether the sensor can detect
    the failure. Returns a bidirectional mapping (fm→sensors, sensor→fms) plus
    the full per-pair relevancy details.

    Note: one LLM call is made per (failure_mode, sensor) pair sequentially.
    Keep both lists small (e.g. ≤5 failure modes, ≤10 sensors) to avoid long
    runtimes. For a chiller with 7 failure modes and 20+ sensors the call will
    take several minutes.

tsfm.name: get_ai_tasks
tsfm.title: Get AI Tasks
tsfm.description:
Returns the list of supported AI task types for time-series analysis.

    Tasks: tsfm_integrated_tsad, tsfm_forecasting, tsfm_forecasting_finetune,
    tsfm_forecasting_evaluation.

tsfm.name: get_tsfm_models
tsfm.title: Get TSFM Models
tsfm.description:
Returns the list of available pre-trained TinyTimeMixer (TTM) model checkpoints.

    Models: ttm_96_28 (context_length=96), ttm_512_96 (context_length=512),
    and energy-domain fine-tuned variants of both.

tsfm.name: run_tsfm_forecasting
tsfm.title: Run TSFM Forecasting
tsfm.description:
Run zero-shot time-series forecasting with a TinyTimeMixer (TTM) model.

    Returns a ForecastingResult whose results_file is the path to a JSON file
    with raw predictions (target_prediction, timestamp, target_columns arrays).
    Pass that path to run_tsad as tsfm_output_json for anomaly detection.

    Args:
        dataset_path: Path to a CSV, JSON, or XLSX dataset.
        timestamp_column: Name of the timestamp column.
        target_columns: Columns to forecast.
        model_checkpoint: Model name (e.g. ttm_96_28) or absolute checkpoint path.
        forecast_horizon: Number of steps to forecast; -1 uses the model default.
        conditional_columns: Exogenous / conditional feature columns.
        id_columns: ID columns for multi-entity grouped time series.
        frequency_sampling: Sampling frequency string (e.g. '15_minutes') or
            'oov' to auto-detect from the data.
        autoregressive_modeling: Use autoregressive inference when True.
        include_dataquality_summary: Attach a data-quality report to the result.

tsfm.name: run_tsfm_finetuning
tsfm.title: Run TSFM Finetuning
tsfm.description:
Few-shot fine-tune a TinyTimeMixer model on a local dataset.

    Returns a FinetuningResult with the saved checkpoint path and a JSON file
    containing per-forecast-horizon performance metrics.

    Args:
        dataset_path: Path to the training dataset (CSV/JSON/XLSX).
        timestamp_column: Name of the timestamp column.
        target_columns: Columns to forecast and fine-tune on.
        model_checkpoint: Base model to start from (e.g. ttm_96_28).
        save_model_dir: Directory to save the fine-tuned model checkpoint.
        forecast_horizon: Steps to forecast; -1 uses the model default.
        n_finetune: Fraction (≤1) or count (>1) of samples for fine-tuning.
        n_calibration: Fraction or count for calibration set (default 0).
        n_test: Fraction or count for test evaluation (default 0.05).
        conditional_columns: Exogenous feature columns.
        id_columns: ID columns for grouped time series.
        frequency_sampling: Sampling frequency string or 'oov' to auto-detect.
        autoregressive_modeling: Use autoregressive mode when True.
        include_dataquality_summary: Attach a data-quality report to the result.

tsfm.name: run_tsad
tsfm.title: Run Anomaly Detection
tsfm.description:
Run conformal anomaly detection on TSFM forecasting output.

    tsfm_output_json must be the results_file path returned by run_tsfm_forecasting.
    Fits (or loads) a conformal AD model and saves anomaly-labelled predictions to CSV.

    Args:
        dataset_path: Path to the original time-series dataset.
        tsfm_output_json: Path to JSON predictions file from run_tsfm_forecasting.
        timestamp_column: Name of the timestamp column.
        target_columns: Target columns that were forecast.
        task: 'fit' to train a new AD model, 'inference' to use an existing one.
        false_alarm: False alarm rate (1 − coverage); default 0.05 → 95% coverage.
        ad_model_type: 'timeseries_conformal' or 'timeseries_conformal_adaptive'.
        ad_model_checkpoint: Path to an existing AD model (required for 'inference').
        ad_model_save: Directory to save the fitted AD model.
        n_calibration: Fraction of data used for calibration (default 0.2).
        conditional_columns: Exogenous feature columns.
        id_columns: ID columns for grouped time series.
        frequency_sampling: Sampling frequency string or None to auto-detect.
        autoregressive_modeling: Use autoregressive mode when True.

tsfm.name: run_integrated_tsad
tsfm.title: Run Integrated Forecasting + Anomaly Detection
tsfm.description:
Run end-to-end time-series forecasting + anomaly detection in one call.

    For each target column: runs zero-shot TTM forecasting, then fits a conformal
    AD model and predicts anomaly labels. Saves a combined CSV with anomaly labels
    and KPI scores for all columns.

    Args:
        dataset_path: Path to the dataset (CSV/JSON/XLSX).
        timestamp_column: Name of the timestamp column.
        target_columns: Columns to run forecasting + anomaly detection on.
        model_checkpoint: Pre-trained TTM model name (default: ttm_96_28).
        false_alarm: False alarm rate; default 0.05 → 95% coverage.
        ad_model_type: 'timeseries_conformal' or 'timeseries_conformal_adaptive'.
        n_calibration: Fraction of data for AD calibration (default 0.2).
        conditional_columns: Exogenous feature columns.
        id_columns: ID columns for grouped time series.
        frequency_sampling: Sampling frequency string or '' to auto-detect.
        autoregressive_modeling: Use autoregressive mode when True.
